guide_feedback: Section 2 precedence vs 'explicit chase' (ids 1246039, 2599962): the clause 'support_followup only when nothing describable is present or the customer explicitly chases' reads as if any chase overrides the precedence chain. Reword to: 'support_followup applies only when the burst contains no describable issue, OR the customer complains about non-response (no one responds / still waiting) with no describable issue. A DM notification (sent you a DM, please check) attached to a describable issue takes the describable intent; the disposition still escalates under rule 6.'

Image-only / link-only first messages and thread_context (ids 2557538, 2118710, 1022726, 822279): state explicitly that image contents and later turns never supply an intent; thread_context may only disambiguate words already present in the first message. Add: 'If the first message text has no diagnosable words, label other/auto (rule 21) even if the thread reveals the real intent later.'

Section 2 'Vague' rule: clarify whether naming 'the app' with no symptom counts as 'device or symptom named -> app' (id 2916575) versus 'no keyword -> other' (id 2557538). Suggested wording: 'Naming the app, a device, or a client counts as device named -> app.'

Unfamiliar-artist recommendations (id 286928): add an example under 'Unfamiliar music' that a same-name / wrong-genre artist appearing in Release Radar or Discover Weekly is feature_request (curation), and that content (metadata) applies only when the customer says tracks are wrongly attributed on a named artist page.

Recurrence wording for downloads loss (id 2582075): the Section 2 list 'second time / always / new phone / after unexplained logout' should add 'keep(s)', 'every time', 'again', and 'all my downloads' so 'why u keep deleting all my downloaded music' unambiguously hits rule 15.

New-device login failure (id 781170): no rule decides between rule 12 (device-scoped, auto) and rule 13 (account, escalate) when the customer has a new phone and no other device is mentioned. Add: 'Login failing on a new phone with both email and Facebook, and no mention of it working elsewhere, is account-scoped -> account_access, escalate. Device-scoped requires the customer to state it works on another device or client.'

Third party signing up with the customer's email (id 1884159): account_security assumes the customer's own account is compromised. Add: 'A stranger creating an account with the customer's email -> account_security; plain first contact and tier unstated -> auto (advise not to verify / claim the address); escalate if the customer states Premium or that their own data is on the account.'
Stolen card / future payment lapse (id 2408812): add to the how_to policy-fact list: 'will Premium be suspended if my card fails / my new card arrives in 10 days' with no charge yet -> how_to, auto.

Server errors on the account/payment page (id 2792171): rule 69 ('logged in + error on payment page -> billing') conflicts with rule 7 (incident -> auto) and rule 12 (web-only -> one rung). Add: 'HTTP 5xx / 503 / 504 on Account or checkout pages while logged in -> billing, escalate, unless an incident is confirmed in the first message; do not apply the web-only rung.'

Missed promo after paying regular price (id 2782168): 'promo charged wrongly' should be widened to 'any charge where the customer says they missed, were denied, or were not applied a promo'; distinguish from feature_request pricing rants (no charge, no eligibility claim).
Unnamed content removal rant (id 2536621): add to content_availability definition: 'requires a named title/artist/podcast; unnamed complaints that Spotify removes songs -> feature_request, auto.'

Profile display-name change (id 153788): add 'profile display name' to the account_access backstage list, and state that an artist asking about their listener profile display name stays account_access, not artist_and_creator.

Third-party platform compromise (id 2627946): clarify that account_security requires the Spotify account itself to be accessed or changed by a third party; a hacked Facebook account needing a Spotify unlink -> account_access, escalate.

Paid-but-not-working after a completed country change (id 982148): strict access > billing precedence would flip to account_access. Add: 'Precedence applies to the primary actionable ask; a completed settings change mentioned as background does not trigger account_access.'

Unlabelable criterion vs other (b): define unlabelable narrowly as (1) promo copy or third-party content with no support ask, (2) a mid-thread reply mistakenly presented as a first message (e.g. device/version info answering an agent, id 598525), (3) no support ask at all. Fragments with any ask remain labelable under other (b).

Stratum tags (targeted:how_to, targeted:praise_or_thanks, targeted:artist) disagree with the guide on several rows (e.g. 298544, 689544, 142167); state in the workflow that stratum tags are sampling metadata and must never be used as a label hint.
PII redaction: state that placeholder tokens such as __email__ or __phone__ in the dataset count as PII present for rule 1 (id 500925).

Rule 21 vs 22 for image-only messages that hint at money (1257204 'updated my details... should I be worried?'): state explicitly that an image-only message with no listed keyword stays rule 21 (auto, clarify) even if it plausibly concerns billing, or add 'details/payment/card' to the Section 2 vague-keyword list if such cases should route to support_followup/escalate.

Capability registry (Section 2) is too short and caused judgment calls: add explicit entries for live radio streams (no), 'play next' (no; queue exists), 'listen later' (no), listener playlist submission to editorial (no), Apple Watch app (no), and state the fallback when the registry is silent (suggest: 'is it possible' questions default to how_to; disposition auto either way).

Vague login question vs suspected outage (446898 'What's up with the log in page?'): clarify that outage-style phrasing about a page/service ('what's up with X', 'is X down') counts as a named symptom -> app (suspected outage), not vague-with-login-keyword -> support_followup, and state whether a thread-confirmed incident may invoke rule 7 when the customer did not use 'known issue' wording.

Rule 8 'someone else's account' is undefined (2455440): specify that it includes a stranger's account created with the customer's email or a report about any account the customer does not own, and that these always escalate because the self-serve hacked-account page cannot resolve them.

Precedence vs 'primary actionable ask' (1756616 locked out + cancel to stop charges): state that the Section 2 precedence order applies even when the customer's explicit request belongs to the lower-ranked intent.

Partner promo trials (818318 vs 669987, 396211): add a line distinguishing 'not yet signed up / trial not applied and not charged -> how_to, auto' from 'signed up and received the wrong trial length or promo -> billing, escalate (partner failure, rule 11)', and state that Groove/Microsoft/Sprint promos count as partner bundles.
Rule 6 (DM request -> escalate) collides with the Section 2 presale fixed line (2580682 'DM me the code'): state that the presale line wins over an incidental DM ask.
Section 2 'Hulu/partner bundle mentioned -> billing, escalate' contradicts rule 10 for pure eligibility questions (167763): state which wins, or narrow the Hulu line to failures/charges only.

Student rule ('charge or expired-on-live-subscription -> billing; otherwise how_to') is ambiguous for renewal-link failures and payment-page updates blocked by student status (1840165, 686630): add 'any failed attempt on a live subscription -> billing, escalate'.
Rule 15 recurrence triggers: list qualifying phrases ('keep', 'each time', 'always', 'again', 'not the first time') so 'keep un-downloading' (642098) is labelled consistently.
Rule 16: clarify that closing the app plus logout/login without a device restart (2682405) does not count as the qualifying logout+restart+login rung.
Rule 14 'chase': define it to include an artist complaining about a delayed submission/release with no prior support contact (1031939), or state that such messages are first-contact auto redirects.

Content tie-break 'named artist won't play' (911629): the definition says 'on every client' but the tie-break does not require the customer to say so; state that unstated client scope defaults to content.

Banter/unlabelable conflict (2507513): the guide treats banter as a valid 'other' intent but the orchestrator's unlabelable definition ('no discernible support ask') flags it; align the two so annotators know whether banter is labelable.

Artist praise with no ask (2032691): Section 1 'other (a) praise/thanks' collides with Section 2 precedence 'artist > other'. Add to the Ownership tie-break: 'An artist/label thanking for placement, playlisting or a feature of their own release -> artist_and_creator, auto (Artist Services redirect); listener thanks -> other'.

Promo/checkout 'won't let me' (559963): the Policy-fact-vs-failure rule lists only 'error message, failed invite, or charge' as billing triggers, so a bare failed attempt with no quoted error was read both ways. Reword to: 'Any stated failed attempt at checkout, promo sign-up or plan join ("won't let me", "keeps failing", "can't apply"), with or without quoted error text -> billing, escalate. Only a pure eligibility/how-to question with no attempt made -> how_to, auto.'

Family invite failure that mentions country/address (2855897): precedence 'access > billing' pulled one annotator to account_access. Add to the Family line: 'Family invite/join/add failures stay billing (rule 11) even when the error mentions country, address or zip/postcode; account_access applies only when the customer explicitly asks to change the country/email of an existing account.'

Vague no-keyword rants and thread_context (1250622, 421932, 538053): the Vague tie-break says 'no keyword -> other' but the batch instructions allow thread_context for disambiguation, and annotators applied it inconsistently. State explicitly: 'If thread_context reveals a device or playback symptom the customer meant, label app_or_playback_issue; the disposition stays auto with one clarifying turn (rule 21). Without such context, label other.'

unlabelable vs praise (275915, 2032691): the task's 'no discernible support ask -> unlabelable' conflicts with the guide listing praise/thanks as a labelable other/auto intent (and with a praise stratum). Add a sentence to Section 0: 'Praise, thanks and banter are labelable (other, auto). Mark unlabelable only for spam, non-English, or indecipherable/image-only content with no recoverable meaning.'

Third-party misuse/licensing reports (1941285) have no home intent. Add to other (d) human-only: 'reports that a venue/business/third party is using Spotify for public performance, or other licensing/ToS reports about someone else -> other, escalate (rule 3)'.

Facebook-to-email migration phrased as a feature request (2517298): the Capability-exists list does not mention Facebook unlink. Add to the registry line: 'Facebook unlink/migration to email is a backstage change -> account_access, escalate, even when phrased as a feature request (access outranks feature).'

Lost password (1831412): rule 13 escalates login/identity but the registry implies self-serve password reset exists. Add: 'Single-account forgotten password with no other complication -> how_to, auto (reset link); lost password across multiple accounts, unknown email, or mobile-number sign-up -> account_access, escalate.'

Rule 5 wording 'Spotify breach claim / phishing needing the email' left 100125 (Spotify-initiated reset after a third-party breach) ambiguous. Reword: 'Customer claims Spotify was breached, questions the legitimacy of a Spotify-initiated reset, or asks whether a specific email is phishing -> account_security, escalate.'

Unknown device vs known co-listener with a named hashtag (2824396 '#timothysipad'): the Pausing tie-break distinguishes 'unknown speaker' from 'known co-listener' but does not say how to treat a named-but-unexplained device. Add: 'A named device/person the customer does not identify as their own household member counts as unknown -> account_security (auto first contact).'

Stratum tags should not be used as label hints; several tags disagreed with the guide-derived intent (1869549 and 1432641 tagged account_access but are billing/security; 1370357 tagged artist but is a listener feature request; 2377282 tagged how_to but is billing; 2008205 tagged praise but is a feature request). Add a note to Section 0: 'Ignore the stratum column when labelling.'

Rules 9/15 vs 19 (2460881): the guide requires Premium to be *stated* but says nothing about Premium being *implied* (prior downloads, 'renewed', 'my premium'). Add to the Tier-unknown rule: 'Evidence that implies but does not state Premium (existing downloads, offline mode) still counts as tier-unknown -> rule 19, one clarifying turn asking whether the subscription is active.'

Precedence vs primary ask (859966): the Section 2 precedence list reads as mechanical, but the orchestrator instruction says 'primary actionable ask', and annotators split. Reword: 'Precedence applies whenever the higher intent is a real, describable symptom or request, even if mentioned second or as an aside; it does not apply to passing mentions with no symptom (e.g. "I'm Premium btw").'

Student tie-break (377561): 'charge or expired-on-live-subscription -> billing' does not say whether a legitimate full-price charge with an implied refund wish counts. Reword: 'a wrongful, disputed or duplicate charge, or an explicit refund demand -> billing, escalate; paying the regular price while eligible for a cheaper plan, with no refund demand -> how_to, auto (explain eligibility and how to switch; never promise a refund).'

Content vs feature for Spotify-made playlists (1867927): add a tie-break under Ownership: 'A specific track missing/removed from any playlist (including Discover Weekly, Daily Mix, editorial) -> content; complaints about what the algorithm chose or the playlist changing as designed -> feature.'

Burst vs customer_message (552679, 1615862): two candidates hold only quote-tweeted Spotify promo copy in customer_message while the actual ask is the second burst tweet in thread_context. Either populate customer_message with the full burst, or add to Section 0: 'If the first tweet is retweeted promo copy, label from the customer's next tweet in the burst; if no burst tweet exists, other(b), rule 21.'

Capability registry is incomplete (2863036, 1615862, 980317, 1950936, 2702293): the 'Capability exists?' list should be extended with a dated (2017) registry entry for: username change (does not exist), PayPal for Student (varies by country, treat as how_to), genre sort/filter of library (does not exist), Apple Watch app (does not exist), iPhone X layout (does not exist). Also state that the registry rule overrides the 'username at sign-up' wording in the account_access definition.

Rule 12 sign-up (2720901): it only covers 'sign-up spinner'; reword to 'any sign-up/account-creation failure with no existing account -> auto, one public rung (other browser/incognito or ask what happens)'; and add to rule 13 that it applies only to *existing* accounts.

Rule 16 'unsupported OS' (2125267): no list is given, so Windows Phone 10 / old iOS could not be adjudicated. Add a short 2017 supported-platform list (iOS 9+, Android 4.1+, Windows 7+, macOS 10.9+, Windows Phone 8.1/10 app present but no longer updated -> still 'supported' for this guide).

Pausing tie-break (2621369): 'used somewhere else' / 'unknown speaker' / 'stops after every song on one device' do not cover random pause/unpause across multiple devices with no attribution. Add: 'Random pausing/unpausing on two or more devices with no attribution -> app, auto, but the clarifying turn must ask whether anyone else has the password (possible shared account).'

Rule 14 artist branches (748111): takedowns, rights, copyright and 'my music is up without permission' fit neither the chase nor the first-contact list. Add: 'Takedown/rights/copyright complaints from the owner -> artist_and_creator, escalate (rule 3 legal also fires).'

Unlabelable definition (1415670, 940661 vs 27956): annotators had to invent the boundary between unlabelable and other(b). State explicitly: 'unlabelable = no discernible support request at all (pure insult, orphan fragment, promo copy with no burst); other(b) = a request is implied but undiagnosable (image-only "you ok?", "it's broken"). Praise is labelable as other(a).'

Rule 12 reset loop (248212): a broken forgot-password web page fixes the disposition (auto, one rung) but not the intent; 'dead login button -> app' suggests app while annotators chose account_access. State: 'password-reset / forgot-password page problems -> account_access_and_settings; login button or web player not loading -> app.'

Explicit chase wording (1933316, 184186): 'nobody will give me a straight answer' and 'no customer service' were treated differently. Reword the support_followup boundary: 'explicit chase means the customer says Spotify (DM, email, support, "you") has not responded; generic "nobody" with a describable symptom stays with the symptom intent; a complaint about the support channel itself with no symptom -> support_followup.'

Rule 22 'tied with different dispositions -> escalate' conflicts with rule 19 'tier-ambiguous tie with billing -> auto' and was cited both ways on 2460881 and 377561. Add: 'Rule 22 applies only after rules 19-21 have been checked; a tie that rule 19 or 21 resolves is not a rule-22 tie.'
